# ubuntu_reboot_barrier Resource

Acts as a Terraform DAG barrier that safely reboots a host and resumes after it returns on a new boot instance.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "ubuntu_reboot_barrier" "example" {
  target = var.host
  reason = "example"
  triggers = { example = "value" }
}
```
## Argument Reference

The resource supports the following arguments:

- `port` (Optional, int64) - Target port for this resource. Overrides provider default_target.port.
- `reason` (Required, string) - Logical reason for the reboot barrier.
- `reboot_command` (Optional, string) - Optional explicit reboot command override.
- `settle_seconds` (Optional, Computed, int64) - Additional settle time after boot proof succeeds.
- `target` (Optional, string) - Target host or address for this resource. Overrides provider default_target.target.
- `timeout_seconds` (Optional, Computed, int64) - Maximum time to wait for reboot and reconnect.
- `transport` (Optional, string) - Transport for this resource. The current provider surface supports ssh.
- `triggers` (Required, map(string)) - Trigger values that cause the reboot barrier to run again when they change.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes:

- `completed_at` (string) - Completion timestamp for the last successful reboot barrier execution.
- `id` (string) - Stable reboot barrier identifier derived from host and reason.
- `last_error` (string) - Last persisted reboot failure detail, if any.
- `operation_id` (string) - Provider-side reboot operation identifier.
- `phase` (string) - Current persisted reboot phase.
- `post_boot_id` (string) - Boot identifier observed after reboot.
- `pre_boot_id` (string) - Boot identifier observed before reboot.
- `stable_host_id` (string) - Stable host identity proven across the reboot.
- `triggers_hash` (string) - Deterministic hash of the trigger map used for state reconciliation.
